newsitem.title: POLAND: Sudzucker may buy more Polish sugar refineries.
newsitem.headline: Sudzucker may buy more Polish sugar refineries.

text.p: The Polish sugar holding which on Friday announced the sale of a stake in one of its major refineries to Sudzucker Gruppe, said it expected the German firm would invest further in southeast Poland.

Lubelsko-Malopolska Spolka Cukrowa said Sudzucker had won a tender for a 38.2 percent stake in the Ropczyce sugar refinery, after it agreed to pay seven zlotys for each of the refinery's seven million new shares -- to total 49 million zlotys.

"The strategic investor (in Ropczyce) is interested in restructuring sugar refineries in southeastern Poland," the president of state-owned Lubelsko-Malopolska, Stanislaw Misztal, told a news conference after the announcement.
"Gaining a German investor could in future prove important for our entire company," Misztal added.
The Polish holding had 51 percent of the shares in Ropczyce, which is located in a town of the same name near the southeastern city of Rzeszow.
After completion of the sale, expected by the end of March, Lubelsko-Malopolska will have 31.5 percent of Ropczyce's shares and the state treasury 30.2 percent.
Ropczyce is one of Poland's largest refineries, with sugar production last year of 58,000 tonnes.

Poland expects to produce a record 2.2-2.25 million tonnes of white sugar in the 1996/97 season against 1.58 million in 1995/96, the head of the Sugar Council grouping sugar refineries said in December.

Misztal said Sudzucker, Europe's biggest beet sugar producer, might participate in the privatisation, expected in 1998, of the entire holding which includes 14 refineries producing about 500,000 tonnes of sugar a year.
"It is not out of the question that Sudzucker will be interested in buying shares in the whole holding at the time when it is launched on the bourse," Misztal said.
In 1995 Poland created four sugar holdings, including Lubelsko-Malopolska, to group around 50 state-owned sugar refineries as a step towards their privatisation.
Poland has 78 sugar refineries, most of which are in state hands, although not all were initially in good enough financial shape to join the holdings.
This compares with almost 180 refineries in the European Union, most of which are much larger than those in Poland.

Other bidders for Ropczyce included Rolimpex, Denmark's Danisco A/S, France's Eridania Beghin-Say, the Netherlands' Cosun and Britain's Tate and Lyle and British Sugar. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
